text: Surviving the first second does not mean you are safe, because the sky itself is about to turn into a blender.

Even though the planet stopped rotating, the entire atmosphere did not get the memo. Hundreds of miles of air keep screaming eastward at over one thousand miles per hour, faster than the speed of sound.

That creates global supersonic shockwaves that strip topsoil off continents, flatten entire cities, and send cars, billboards, and shipping containers tumbling through the air like dry leaves in a hurricane.

Friction between that roaring wall of wind and the stationary ground generates unimaginable heat and static electricity. Massive firestorms spark across dry forests while thunderclouds tear themselves apart.
If you somehow ducked into a deep subway tunnel to wait it out, congratulations—you avoided the flying sedans, only to hear the sound of a global sonic boom rattling your fillings.
